es: Distinguir en un texto de estudio breve la afirmación (claim), la prueba (evidence) y la opinión, reconociendo las expresiones que señalan cada una.

vocabulary.es: pruebas, datos que apoyan una idea

teaching.en: The claim is that schools should start later in the morning.
teaching.es: La afirmación es que los colegios deberían empezar más tarde por la mañana.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim es la idea que el autor defiende y quiere que aceptes.
segments: The claim is that schools should
start later in the morning.
teaching.audioText: The claim is that schools should start later in the morning.

teaching.en: According to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under seven hours.
teaching.es: Según una encuesta a 300 estudiantes, la mayoría duerme menos de siete horas.
teaching.explanationEs: La prueba cita una fuente (according to) y un dato concreto (300 students).
segments: According to a survey of 300 students,
most of them sleep under seven hours.
teaching.audioText: According to a survey of 300 students, most of them sleep under seven hours.

teaching.en: The data show that test scores went up by ten percent.
teaching.es: Los datos muestran que las notas subieron un diez por ciento.
teaching.explanationEs: Data show: los datos son una prueba porque se pueden comprobar.
segments: The data show that test scores
went up by ten percent.
teaching.audioText: The data show that test scores went up by ten percent.

teaching.en: Some experts argue that teenagers need more sleep.
teaching.es: Algunos expertos sostienen que los adolescentes necesitan dormir más.
teaching.explanationEs: Argue that + idea presenta lo que defiende alguien; todavía no es una prueba.
segments: Some experts argue that
teenagers need more sleep.
teaching.audioText: Some experts argue that teenagers need more sleep.

teaching.en: In my opinion, mornings are too early for teenagers.
teaching.es: En mi opinión, las mañanas son demasiado tempranas para los adolescentes.
teaching.explanationEs: In my opinion, I think, I feel: marcan un juicio personal sin datos.
segments: In my opinion, mornings are
too early for teenagers.
teaching.audioText: In my opinion, mornings are too early for teenagers.

teaching.en: It is a fact that 300 students answered the survey, but it is only an opinion that mornings are boring.
teaching.es: Es un hecho que 300 estudiantes respondieron la encuesta, pero es solo una opinión que las mañanas son aburridas.
teaching.explanationEs: Un hecho se puede comprobar; una opinión expresa un gusto o una valoración.
segments: It is a fact that 300 students answered the survey,
but it is only an opinion that mornings are boring.
teaching.audioText: It is a fact that 300 students answered the survey, but it is only an opinion that mornings are boring.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que funciona como prueba en el texto.

choices.text: According to a survey of 300 students, 68 percent sleep under seven hours.
Teenagers need more sleep.
I feel tired every morning.

feedback.es: La prueba cita una fuente (a survey of 300 students) y un dato comprobable (68 percent). Teenagers need more sleep es la afirmación, e I feel tired es una opinión personal.

hint.es: Busca la frase que nombra una fuente y da una cifra.

origin.text: Teenagers need more sleep. According to a survey of 300 students, 68 percent sleep under seven hours. I feel tired every morning.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los datos muestran que las notas subieron.»

feedback.es: Data es el sustantivo de los datos que se recogen en un estudio; The data show that… introduce una prueba comprobable.

hint.es: Son las cifras que se recogen en un estudio.

origin.text: The ___ show that test scores went up.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Muchos profesores sostienen que los deberes ayudan a aprender.»

answer.text: Many teachers argue that homework helps students learn

feedback.es: Many teachers argue that + idea presenta la afirmación de un grupo; después viene la idea completa: homework helps students learn.

hint.es: Empieza con Many teachers y sigue con argue that.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con su función en un texto de estudio.

pairs: The claim is that cities need more parks.
A survey of 500 people found that 70 percent want more trees.
In my opinion, parks are relaxing.

feedback.es: La afirmación defiende una idea general, la prueba aporta una fuente y una cifra, y la opinión expresa un juicio personal con in my opinion.

pairs: The claim is that cities need more parks.
A survey of 500 people found that 70 percent want more trees.
In my opinion, parks are relaxing.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué prueba se da a favor de la afirmación.

choices.text: Experts say that children learn slowly.
In a study, the pupils got better reading results.
The speaker thinks language classes are boring.

feedback.es: La prueba es el estudio de cuatrocientos alumnos con mejores resultados de lectura; lo que dicen los expertos es la afirmación que esa prueba apoya.

origin.audio: Some experts argue that children should start a second language early. A study of four hundred pupils found that they scored higher in reading tests.

prompt.es: Completa: «Según una encuesta, el 60 % prefiere estudiar de noche.»

feedback.es: According to + fuente (a survey) introduce una prueba; no sirve para dar tu propia opinión.

origin.text: ___ to a survey, 60 percent prefer to study at night.

prompt.es: Elige la oración que expresa una opinión, no una afirmación ni una prueba.

choices.text: Reading on paper is better for memory.
A study of 120 students found that paper readers remembered 15 percent more details.
I think paper books are more beautiful.

feedback.es: I think + un gusto personal («more beautiful») no se puede comprobar: es una opinión. Better for memory es la afirmación y el estudio de 120 estudiantes es la prueba.

origin.text: Reading on paper is better for memory. A study of 120 students found that paper readers remembered 15 percent more details. I think paper books are more beautiful.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la afirmación principal del informe.

choices.text: Cycling to work can lower stress.
Most workers dislike cycling.
Surveys are not reliable.

feedback.es: La afirmación es que ir en bici al trabajo reduce el estrés; la encuesta del 72 % es solo la prueba que la apoya.

origin.audio: The report claims that cycling to work reduces stress. To support this, it gives a survey in which seventy-two percent of cyclists said they felt calm.

prompt.es: Completa: «Hay pruebas sólidas de que el sueño ayuda a la memoria.»

feedback.es: Evidence es incontable: se dice strong evidence, sin plural ni a, y con there is.

origin.text: There is strong ___ that sleep helps memory.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los datos muestran que el uso del transporte público aumentó.»

answer.text: The data show that public transport use increased

feedback.es: The data show that + resultado presenta una prueba: el sujeto son los datos y el resultado va después de that.

prompt.es: Clasifica la oración del texto: ¿claim, evidence u opinion?

choices.text: claim
evidence
opinion

feedback.es: Una cifra concreta atribuida a una investigación es una prueba porque se puede comprobar; una afirmación defendería una idea general y una opinión llevaría I think.

origin.text: Research shows that 40 percent of adults read every day.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué frase del audio es una prueba.

choices.text: The speaker wants museums to cost nothing.
The council wants more visitors.
The number of families went up by twenty percent.

feedback.es: La prueba son las cifras del año pasado: un aumento del veinte por ciento en familias. Las otras dos ideas son una opinión y una afirmación ajena.

origin.audio: In my opinion, museums should be free. The city council argues that free entry would bring more visitors, and last year's figures show a twenty percent rise in families.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con lo que introduce.

feedback.es: The data show that introduce un resultado comprobable, Experts argue that presenta la tesis de otros e I believe that marca una opinión propia.

es: Matizar afirmaciones académicas con verbos, modales y expresiones de cautela (may indicate, it could be argued, to a certain extent, there is limited evidence) sin exagerar lo que permiten los datos.

teaching.en: The findings may indicate that short naps improve memory.
teaching.es: Los resultados podrían indicar que las siestas cortas mejoran la memoria.
teaching.explanationEs: May + indicate: los datos apuntan en una dirección, pero no lo prueban.
segments: The findings may indicate that
short naps improve memory.
teaching.audioText: The findings may indicate that short naps improve memory.

teaching.en: It could be argued that homework has a limited effect on learning.
teaching.es: Se podría argumentar que los deberes tienen un efecto limitado en el aprendizaje.
teaching.explanationEs: It could be argued that presenta una idea defendible sin afirmarla como un hecho.
segments: It could be argued that homework
has a limited effect on learning.
teaching.audioText: It could be argued that homework has a limited effect on learning.

teaching.en: To a certain extent, online classes help students who work.
teaching.es: En cierta medida, las clases en línea ayudan a los estudiantes que trabajan.
teaching.explanationEs: To a certain extent limita la afirmación: es verdad solo hasta cierto punto.
segments: To a certain extent, online
classes help students who work.
teaching.audioText: To a certain extent, online classes help students who work.

teaching.en: The results suggest that most students prefer quiet places.
teaching.es: Los resultados sugieren que la mayoría de los estudiantes prefiere los lugares tranquilos.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest that + idea: verbo de cautela muy frecuente en los informes.
segments: The results suggest that most
students prefer quiet places.
teaching.audioText: The results suggest that most students prefer quiet places.

teaching.en: Teenagers tend to sleep later than adults, which is largely due to biology.
teaching.es: Los adolescentes suelen dormir más tarde que los adultos, lo cual se debe en gran parte a la biología.
teaching.explanationEs: Tend to + verbo base expresa una tendencia; largely reduce la certeza sobre la causa.
segments: Teenagers tend to sleep later than adults,
which is largely due to biology.
teaching.audioText: Teenagers tend to sleep later than adults, which is largely due to biology.

teaching.en: Memory is likely to improve with regular sleep.
teaching.es: Es probable que la memoria mejore con un sueño regular.
teaching.explanationEs: Be likely to + verbo base: probabilidad, no seguridad.
segments: Memory is likely to
improve with regular sleep.
teaching.audioText: Memory is likely to improve with regular sleep.

prompt.es: Elige la versión con cautela de: «Naps improve memory.»

choices.text: The results prove that naps improve memory.
The results suggest that naps improve memory.
Naps improve memory for everyone.

feedback.es: The results suggest that… apunta a una conclusión sin cerrarla. Prove y for everyone exageran lo que puede afirmar un estudio.

hint.es: Busca un verbo que apunte en una dirección sin cerrar la cuestión.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los adolescentes tienden a dormir más tarde.»

feedback.es: Tend to + verbo base expresa una tendencia general; con teenagers el verbo no lleva -s.

hint.es: Verbo que significa «tender a», sin -s con teenagers.

origin.text: Teenagers ___ to sleep later.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En cierta medida, los deberes ayudan a aprender.»

answer.text: To a certain extent homework helps students learn

feedback.es: To a certain extent abre la frase y limita la afirmación; después viene la idea: homework helps students learn.

hint.es: Empieza con la expresión To a certain extent.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que matiza sin exagerar lo que permiten los datos.

choices.text: Yoga definitely solves sleep problems.
Yoga has no effect on sleep at all.
Yoga may improve sleep, but the evidence is limited.

feedback.es: Con un estudio pequeño, may improve y the evidence is limited describen justo lo que se sabe. Solves y no effect at all afirman mucho más de lo que muestran los datos.

origin.text: A small study of 25 adults found better sleep after yoga.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué conclusión se puede sacar del audio.

choices.text: Music may help attention a little.
Music clearly harms attention.
The study proves that music always helps.

feedback.es: El audio dice que los resultados parecen mostrar un efecto pequeño y probable: por eso la conclusión cauta es que la música podría ayudar un poco.

origin.audio: The study included only thirty students, so the results should be read with care. They appear to show that music helps attention, but the effect is probably small.

prompt.es: Completa las dos frases con un verbo o un adverbio de cautela.

feedback.es: Suggest (o indicate) es el verbo de cautela que introduce el resultado; largely, mostly o mainly marcan que la causa es solo en gran parte.

sentences: The results ___ that coffee improves attention.
Sleep problems are ___ caused by stress, but not always.

prompt.es: Elige la versión más cautelosa y correcta de la afirmación del autor.

choices.text: The findings prove that this diet stops all headaches.
The findings suggest that this diet may reduce headaches in some people.
This diet stops headaches, according to 30 people.

feedback.es: Suggest that + may reduce ajusta la conclusión a 30 personas: dice que podría ocurrir en algunas. Prove y all headaches exageran más allá de lo que sostienen los datos.

origin.text: Claim: «This diet stops headaches.» The study followed 30 people for two weeks.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué piensa la autora sobre los cursos cortos.

choices.text: Short courses are proven to work better.
Long courses are impossible to teach.
The benefit of short courses is not well supported.

feedback.es: La autora dice que se podría argumentar a favor de los cursos cortos, pero que hay pruebas limitadas de que los estudiantes aprendan más: su postura es cauta.

origin.audio: It could be argued that schools should offer shorter courses. However, there is limited evidence that students learn more in shorter courses.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los resultados indican que los gatos duermen más que los perros.»

feedback.es: Indicate (o suggest) es un verbo de cautela para presentar un resultado sin afirmarlo como hecho absoluto.

origin.text: The results ___ that cats sleep longer than dogs.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hay pocas pruebas de que este método funcione en adultos.»

answer.text: There is limited evidence that this method works for adults

feedback.es: There is limited evidence that + idea es la fórmula para decir que las pruebas son escasas; evidence es incontable y va con is.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que exagera lo que permiten los datos.

choices.text: Everyone in the country prefers tea.
Most of the people surveyed preferred tea.
The survey suggests that tea may be popular.

feedback.es: Una encuesta a 54 personas no permite hablar de todo el país: Everyone exagera. Las otras frases se limitan a la muestra o usan suggests y may.

origin.text: A survey of 54 people found that 60 percent prefer tea.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión de cautela con su significado.

feedback.es: Cada expresión matiza de una forma: tend to habla de costumbre, to a certain extent de grado, limited evidence de pocas pruebas y largely de la mayor parte.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué dice el hablante sobre los adolescentes.

choices.text: All of them go to bed late because of homework.
Many go to bed late, partly for social reasons.
Few of them sleep at night.

feedback.es: Studies indicate y tend to son verbos de cautela: hablan de muchos adolescentes, no de todos, y partly señala que la causa social es solo una parte.

origin.audio: Studies indicate that most teenagers tend to go to bed late. The reasons are partly social.

es: Leer un resumen académico (abstract) e identificar su objetivo, su método y su conclusión cautelosa, apoyándote en las señales de cada parte.

teaching.en: An abstract is a short summary of a study, and it usually follows the order aim, method and conclusion.
teaching.es: Un resumen académico es una síntesis breve de un estudio y suele seguir el orden objetivo, método y conclusión.
teaching.explanationEs: Abstract: el resumen al principio de un artículo; conviene leerlo en orden.
segments: An abstract is a short summary of a study, and
it usually follows the order aim, method and conclusion.
teaching.audioText: An abstract is a short summary of a study, and it usually follows the order aim, method and conclusion.

teaching.en: The aim of this study is to examine how sleep affects exam performance.
teaching.es: El objetivo de este estudio es examinar cómo afecta el sueño al rendimiento en los exámenes.
teaching.explanationEs: The aim is to + verbo: señal del objetivo (por qué se hizo el estudio).
segments: The aim of this study is to
examine how sleep affects exam performance.
teaching.audioText: The aim of this study is to examine how sleep affects exam performance.

teaching.en: The sample included 120 participants aged between 16 and 18.
teaching.es: La muestra incluyó a 120 participantes de entre 16 y 18 años.
teaching.explanationEs: Sample y participants señalan el método: quién fue estudiado.
segments: The sample included 120 participants
aged between 16 and 18.
teaching.audioText: The sample included 120 participants aged between 16 and 18.

teaching.en: The method was simple: each group followed a different sleep schedule for two weeks.
teaching.es: El método fue sencillo: cada grupo siguió un horario de sueño distinto durante dos semanas.
teaching.explanationEs: Method: cómo se hizo el estudio (grupos, duración, instrumentos).
segments: The method was simple: each group followed
a different sleep schedule for two weeks.
teaching.audioText: The method was simple: each group followed a different sleep schedule for two weeks.

teaching.en: The group with more sleep had a higher score in memory tests.
teaching.es: El grupo que durmió más obtuvo una puntuación más alta en las pruebas de memoria.
teaching.explanationEs: Score: el resultado medible; los resultados van antes de la conclusión.
segments: The group with more sleep had
a higher score in memory tests.
teaching.audioText: The group with more sleep had a higher score in memory tests.

teaching.en: The authors conclude that more sleep may improve performance, although more research is needed.
teaching.es: Los autores concluyen que dormir más podría mejorar el rendimiento, aunque hace falta más investigación.
teaching.explanationEs: Conclude that + idea con cautela (may, although…): señal de la conclusión.
segments: The authors conclude that more sleep may
improve performance, although more research is needed.
teaching.audioText: The authors conclude that more sleep may improve performance, although more research is needed.

feedback.es: The authors conclude that + idea con may es la señal de la conclusión cautelosa: la música tranquila podría ayudar.

The authors conclude that diet may affect mood.

Walking to school clearly improves attention.
Pupils who walk to school pay less attention.

Whether reading before bed improves sleep.
How many hours adults sleep in winter.

aim
conclusion

es: Escribir un párrafo académico sobre hábitos de estudio con una afirmación clara, evidencia concreta y una conclusión matizada con tres recursos de cautela de tipos distintos.

teaching.en: A good paragraph starts with a claim and supports it with evidence.
teaching.es: Un buen párrafo empieza con una afirmación y la apoya con pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: El párrafo académico sigue el orden afirmación, evidencia y conclusión.
segments: A good paragraph starts with a
claim and supports it with evidence.
teaching.audioText: A good paragraph starts with a claim and supports it with evidence.

teaching.en: A short study session every day may be more effective than one long night.
teaching.es: Una sesión de estudio corta cada día puede ser más eficaz que una noche larga.
teaching.explanationEs: Session y effective: may be + adjetivo matiza la afirmación.
segments: A short study session every day may
be more effective than one long night.
teaching.audioText: A short study session every day may be more effective than one long night.

teaching.en: A survey suggests that students who review their notes regularly remember more.
teaching.es: Una encuesta sugiere que los estudiantes que repasan sus apuntes con regularidad recuerdan más.
teaching.explanationEs: La evidencia va con una fuente y suggests es un verbo de cautela.
segments: A survey suggests that students who
review their notes regularly remember more.
teaching.audioText: A survey suggests that students who review their notes regularly remember more.

teaching.en: The effect may depend on the subject, so the writer avoids absolute words.
teaching.es: El efecto puede depender de la asignatura, así que el autor evita las palabras absolutas.
teaching.explanationEs: Depend on + nombre: el matiz explica de qué depende el resultado.
segments: The effect may depend on the subject,
so the writer avoids absolute words.
teaching.audioText: The effect may depend on the subject, so the writer avoids absolute words.

teaching.en: The paragraph ends with a cautious conclusion: regular practice seems to help most students.
teaching.es: El párrafo termina con una conclusión cautelosa: la práctica regular parece ayudar a la mayoría de los estudiantes.
teaching.explanationEs: Seems to help y most students: la conclusión no dice «todos».
segments: The paragraph ends with a cautious conclusion:
regular practice seems to help most students.
teaching.audioText: The paragraph ends with a cautious conclusion: regular practice seems to help most students.

teaching.en: A regular schedule is likely to be a better habit than one long night before an exam.
teaching.es: Un horario regular probablemente sea mejor hábito que una noche larga antes de un examen.
teaching.explanationEs: Be likely to + verbo base cierra el párrafo con probabilidad, no con certeza.
segments: A regular schedule is likely to be a better
habit than one long night before an exam.
teaching.audioText: A regular schedule is likely to be a better habit than one long night before an exam.

prompt.es: Elige la mejor frase de apertura (afirmación) para un párrafo sobre hábitos.

choices.text: Short study sessions may be more effective than long ones.
I love studying every day, so sessions are great.
A survey of 200 students was carried out in June.

feedback.es: La afirmación de apertura expresa la idea principal con cautela (may be). Una cifra suelta es evidencia y un gusto personal es una opinión.

hint.es: La afirmación es la idea principal: lleva cautela y no empieza con una cifra.

prompt.es: Completa: «El efecto puede depender de la asignatura.»

feedback.es: Depend va siempre con on: depend on the subject. Después del modal may el verbo va en forma base.

hint.es: Verbo que se construye con on.

origin.text: The effect may ___ on the subject.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Esto sugiere que repasar con regularidad ayuda.»

answer.text: This suggests that reviewing regularly helps

feedback.es: This suggests that + idea es una conclusión cautelosa: el verbo suggests apunta sin afirmar; reviewing regularly es el sujeto de helps.

prompt.es: Elige la conclusión con un solo recurso de cautela bien usado.

choices.text: Perhaps this may possibly suggest that daily review might help.
This suggests that daily review may help.

prompt.es: Escribe un párrafo sobre hábitos de estudio con cautela.

answer.text: Many students believe that long study nights are the best way to prepare for exams, but research suggests that regular short sessions may be more effective. A survey of 200 college students found that those who studied for forty minutes every day scored ten percent higher than those who studied only before the exam. This appears to show that regular review helps memory, although the effect may depend on the subject. For example, languages and science seem to benefit more from daily practice than essay subjects. It could be argued that students who study every day are simply more interested in studying, so the results should be read with care. To a certain extent, a good schedule matters more than the number of hours. In conclusion, a short session every day is likely to be a better habit than one long night, but more research is needed.
accepted: Many students believe that long study nights are the best way to prepare for exams, but research suggests that regular short sessions may be more effective. A survey of 200 college students found that those who studied for forty minutes every day scored ten percent higher than those who studied only before the exam. This appears to show that regular review helps memory, although the effect may depend on the subject. For example, languages and science seem to benefit more from daily practice than essay subjects. It could be argued that students who study every day are simply more interested in studying, so the results should be read with care. To a certain extent, a good schedule matters more than the number of hours. In conclusion, a short session every day is likely to be a better habit than one long night, but more research is needed.

Some people think that listening to music while studying improves concentration. However, a study of 120 teenagers suggests that silence may be better for difficult tasks. The teenagers who worked in a quiet room scored eight percent higher on a reading test than those who listened to music. This seems to indicate that music can distract students, although it might help with simple tasks such as copying notes. It could be argued that some students are used to music and feel calmer with it, so the effect may depend on the person. Largely for this reason, the results should be read with care. Nevertheless, there is some evidence that a quiet schedule with short sessions is likely to work better for most students.

title.en: Present findings to a study group
title.es: Presentar hallazgos a un grupo de estudio

es: Presentar ante un grupo de estudio los hallazgos de un estudio: resumirlos con fidelidad, dar una conclusión cautelosa y responder a una objeción reconociendo sus límites.

prompt.es: Escribe tu presentación: resume, concluye con cautela y responde.

answer.text: Good morning, everyone. Let me summarise our study. One hundred and fifty students kept a study diary for a month. The students who reviewed their notes every day scored twelve percent higher in a final test than the others. The findings suggest that daily review may help students remember more, and this seems to be true for most subjects. Some of you may have an objection, so let me reply to one of them: a classmate said that these students were probably more interested already. That is a fair point, and it is a limitation of the study. To a certain extent, you may be right. Nevertheless, the difference was large, and it is likely to be valid for students of our age. More research is needed before we can be sure, but I would suggest trying daily review this month. Thank you for listening.
accepted: Good morning, everyone. Let me summarise our study. One hundred and fifty students kept a study diary for a month. The students who reviewed their notes every day scored twelve percent higher in a final test than the others. The findings suggest that daily review may help students remember more, and this seems to be true for most subjects. Some of you may have an objection, so let me reply to one of them: a classmate said that these students were probably more interested already. That is a fair point, and it is a limitation of the study. To a certain extent, you may be right. Nevertheless, the difference was large, and it is likely to be valid for students of our age. More research is needed before we can be sure, but I would suggest trying daily review this month. Thank you for listening.

Hello, everyone. To summarise, 150 students wrote in a study diary every day for a month. After the month, the students who reviewed their notes daily scored twelve percent higher in the final test. The results suggest that regular review might improve memory. Someone has asked whether these students were already more interested. That is a good point, and I accept it as a limitation. It could be argued that interested students simply study more. However, the findings still seem to show a clear effect, so I think the conclusion is likely to be valid, although we need more research. For now, I would suggest that we all try daily review for one month, and then compare our scores. Thank you for your attention.
